transcript.text: “Not working” can mean a few quite different faults: no power or a door/control issue if it will not start at all; restricted airflow if it runs but stops or dries badly; or a heating fault if the drum turns but there is no warmth. First, please tell me what happens when you select a programme and press Start: are there any display lights, does the drum turn, or is it completely dead? If there is an error code, include that too. Before further testing, make sure the door closes firmly and the machine is plugged directly into a working wall socket rather than an extension lead.
Lights come on but when I press start nothing happens, no sound and the drum doesn't turn. No error code. It's been like this since this morning.

A broken belt is less likely than a start-permission fault: most commonly the door catch/interlock is not registering as shut. A stiff or jammed drum can also prevent starting; if both are normal, the start/control circuit becomes more likely. 1. Switch off and unplug the dryer. Check the door catch and the slot it closes into for fluff, a loose catch, or damage. Close the empty door firmly: it should latch positively. A weak latch or no positive click points to the door catch/interlock.
2. With it still unplugged and empty, turn the drum by hand. It should move smoothly with some normal resistance. If it is stiff, stuck, grinding, or very loose, do not keep trying to start it; that points to a drum support/obstruction issue. If the latch feels positive and the drum turns normally, this is more likely an internal interlock, control or wiring fault and is usually an engineer job rather than a part to guess at.
Door doesn't click shut, it swings back slightly open. The plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, I found the piece on the floor. Drum I haven't turned by hand yet.

The snapped plastic tongue is very likely the reason it will not start. The dryer needs the door to latch properly so it can operate the door safety switch; with the tongue missing, it cannot do that. 1. Switch off and unplug it. Do not try to wedge, tape or bypass the door closed—this safety switch is there to stop the dryer running with the door open.
2. Check that no fabric or fluff is caught around the door opening, and look for obvious hinge damage or a door sitting out of line. If it is simply the broken tongue/catch and the door otherwise aligns properly, the usual repair is the mechanical door handle/catch assembly.
3. While it is unplugged and empty, turn the drum by hand as previously suggested. This is separate from the no-start fault, but a smooth normal turn would make an additional drum problem unlikely. If the door still will not stay shut after the mechanical catch is repaired, the next suspect would be the door interlock/switch or its wiring, which is normally an engineer repair. At present, though, the visibly broken catch is the clear first fault.
